Not built - needs a maintainer look. No blockers found on the read.

This head adds SPLINE and ELLIPSE reading to the DXF import, new fit-point validation, the provenance cleanup, and a new wire golden. I read the full diff (30 files) against the laws in AGENTS.md.

What looks good:
- The change is carefully scoped to geometry: no commands, no UI, no schema, no new dependencies, no process files, no `.github`, no `build.rs`, no snapshot PNGs.
- Each new module (`biarc.rs`, `curve_fit.rs`, `curves.rs`, `nurbs.rs`) carries a one-line provenance comment, and the new test files sit in the existing `dxf/` directory suite with the fixture files beside them.
- Degenerate input is refused by name, not clamped: degree 1-11, knot count and multiplicity, weight count/positivity/ratio, Z-plane rules for both control and fit points (each point gets one Z, an omitted Z is 0), parameter range for ellipses and parameter over 1e6, the evaluation budget (50M), cusp refusal after 40 halvings, and the > 1000 mm arc that becomes a line.
- The fit-point fix (1359ef98e) mirrors the control-point rule of 62b3fdf17 exactly: `finish_fit` (crates/geometry/src/dxf/curves.rs:210) checks one Z per point, refuses orphan/duplicate Z and Y-before-X, and requires all fit and control points in one Z plane. The new tests (`spline_fit_points_use_a_per_point_z_default`, `spline_fit_points_refuse_orphan_and_duplicate_z`) pin both sides.
- `SketchData::from_dxf` refuses a drawing whose applied unit loosens the bound past 1 µm (crates/geometry/src/sketch_data.rs:118), with a refusal that names `$INSUNITS`. The check is honest about a unitless drawing read in metres.
- The ELLIPSE "round" path is bounded by the tolerance, not a fixed ratio threshold: ratio 1.0 stays an exact circle with no tolerance recorded; a near-round ellipse is recorded in `curve_tolerance` only while the circle is within the bound (crates/geometry/src/dxf/curves.rs:126-137).
- INSERT and POINT are skipped and counted, and the rest of the drawing reads; a selected-chain wire cut still refuses a drawing with a skipped INSERT/POINT by name, as for HATCH.
- The new golden (wire-iso/wire_dxf_spline_die.nc) has the documented purpose (spline as tangent arcs), the golden count is plausible (73 G3 blocks, 74 G1 lines), and the PR body documents the known zero-length-G1 defect with a follow-up. The provenance cleanup in `crates/post/src/agie*` rewrites lines, not code, and retains the MIT licence text.

Results merged with main: NOT BUILT on this host. The trial merge is clean (`git merge --no-ff --no-commit origin/main` auto-merged `crates/app/tests/wire_dxf_selection/arcs.rs` with no conflicts, 172 files staged, no conflicts markers; PR head is MERGEABLE). The local build cannot run here: this host has no C compiler (`cc` is absent; `apt-get install gcc` is refused with a dpkg lock), so the xtask dry-run dies at the `crc32fast` build script, before any workspace code compiles. The PR-test runner path does not apply: this is a fork PR (author qsmits is not a collaborator), so it must build locally (step 2b).

Targeted tests: not run. The PR body names the pinning tests and the quick gate as green at head 1359ef98e (quick: 1206 steps, 0 failed; strict clippy clean; light lane 5 steps; dxf suites green). I could not verify any of that. The light lane and the example catalog suites are owed at review (geometry-only diff, no post/toolpath change; no heavy step is owed, issue #1865 is P4). The author should confirm the quick gate and the dxf suites on this head before merge.

Requested before merge:
1. Run the quick gate (and the example catalog / wire_dxf_selection suites) on the current head and post the result, or the maintainer re-runs them. The build cannot run on this host and is not verified by this review.
2. Only if a gate run is green: merge as the maintainer's call. Do not merge on this review alone.

Questions / notes (not blocking):
- The provenance cleanup rewrites the Agie licence/provenance lines to say "our own earlier implementation" and removes the mention of the tool the JEScript attributes were documented by (assets/ui/LICENSES.md:463, site/static/icons/LICENSES.txt, crates/post/src/agie/{mod,cutoff,group}.rs, crates/post/src/agie_setup.rs, crates/post/src/agie_setup/{cutoff,group,quality}.rs, crates/post/src/agie_setup/inspection/piece.rs, docs/decisions/2966-agie-fine-quality.md). The MIT copyright text is retained, so the licence condition stands. The wording change records where the JEScript settings came from, which is a factual claim; worth a maintainer look before merge.
- The PR body says "74 G3 blocks" for the spline die; the golden contains 73 G3 (the initial G1 line and 74 G1s). Cosmetic.
- The PR body says the effort is `effort:high` while the issue is labelled `effort:max`. Cosmetic.
- The `arcs.rs` hunk (start -> `picks`) is carried from PR #3953, which is already merged; the trial merge resolves it cleanly.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

Not built - needs a maintainer look. No blockers found on the read. The geometry half of this PR is built and green locally; the app half cannot be built on this host (no C compiler, see below).

What looks good:
- The change is carefully scoped to geometry: no commands, no UI, no schema, no new dependencies, no process files, no `.github`, no `build.rs`, no snapshot PNGs, no test-binary changes outside `crates/geometry/tests/dxf/`.
- The new modules (`biarc.rs`, `curve_fit.rs`, `curves.rs`, `nurbs.rs`) each carry a one-line provenance comment, stay under 400 lines, and refuse bad data by name (degree, knot count and multiplicity, weights, Z plane, extrusion, parameter ranges, budget) instead of clamping.
- The fit is genuinely two-sided: a coarse pass, a dense Hausdorff check (curve points to the output, output points to the curve with a gap bound), plus a speed bound that covers the curve side between samples. The non-rational spline bound is the derivative control polygon, and the code comment records the formula and its source.
- The new golden (`wire-iso/wire_dxf_spline_die.nc`) is one file, new, explained in the body, read line by line: 73 `G3` blocks, lead-in/lead-out `G1`s and one `G0`. All existing goldens unchanged, which the body states.
- The tests join the existing directory suites (`crates/geometry/tests/dxf/`), the refusal tests use a fixed-seed mutation loop, and `test_harness`-level code is untouched.

Results merged with main. Trial merge: clean - `origin/main` (d80dc6944) is an ancestor of the branch; `git merge --no-ff --no-commit origin/main` reports "Already up to date". The `--delta 3958 --reviewed 1359ef98e` verdict is NEW CODE (the merge commit `641ac0448`, the golden commit `1e9840209`, the provenance commit `ae5b858f5`), so this review covers the head, not just the new commits.

Locally on this host (Linux, worktree `.claude/worktrees/cc-pr3958-review`):
- `cargo test -p camcraft-geometry --test dxf`: 23/23 pass.
- `cargo test -p camcraft-geometry --test dxf_refusals`: 25/25 pass (`dxf_refusals`, `curve_bounds`, `curve_refusals`).
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-geometry --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- The new tests are the pinning tests named in the body (`closed_cubic_spline_reads_as_tangent_arcs_within_the_bound`, `rational_quarter_circle_spline_becomes_arcs_on_its_circle`, `degree_one_spline_is_its_control_polygon`, `ellipses_read_as_tangent_arcs_and_a_round_one_stays_a_circle`, `a_slender_ellipse_keeps_the_bound_at_its_tight_ends`, `insert_and_point_are_skipped_and_the_rest_reads`, and the `curve_refusals`/`curve_bounds` cases) and they passed.

Not run locally (this host has no C compiler):
- `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test wire_dxf_selection` - the new spline golden test and the INSERT refusal cannot build. The `ring` crate, a dependency of `camcraft-app` (via `reqwest`/`rustls`), cannot compile its C sources:

```text
error occurred in cc-rs: command did not execute successfully (status code exit status: 1): "cc" "-O1" ... "-o" ".../ring/.../25ac62e5b3c53843-curve25519.o" "-c" ".../ring-0.17.14/crypto/curve25519/curve25519.c"
```

and `cc` in this host (`/tmp/toolchain/prefix/usr/bin/cc`) reports `x86_64-linux-gnu-gcc-15: fatal error: cannot execute 'cc1': posix_spawnp: No such file or directory`. There is no `cc1` anywhere on the host and no other C compiler.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` - the same wall stops the build.
- `cargo xtask gate light` - needs the release build of `camcraft-app`; not run for the same reason.

The author's own gate on this head (PR body, `ae5b858f5`): quick 1212 steps, 0 failed; strict clippy clean; light lane 5 steps 0 failed. The runner path (step 2b) was not available: the author `qsmits` is not a collaborator with push access, so this is reviewed locally, and the author's macOS run is cited, not re-run.

Targeted tests: no post or toolpath change in the diff (the `crates/post` changes are one-line provenance comment rewrites only), so no example catalog suites are owed. The wire_dxf_selection suite - the suite that pins the new golden - is not run here (see above). Light lane is not run (see above). No `P1`/`P2`/`P3` issue is claimed by this PR (`P4` enhancement), so no targeted heavy step is owed.

Requested before merge: none found on the read.

Notes:
- The `refs`-form ending (`Refs #3937`, `Refs #1865`) is correct: #1865 stays open for block expansion and the fit-point interpolation gap is documented as a dropped item.
- The license heading and LICENSES text: the MIT licence text is kept verbatim in `assets/ui/LICENSES.md` and `site/static/icons/LICENSES.txt`; only the heading line and "documented by Agie Processor" were renamed to our own implementation. Worth a maintainer's eye on the licence file, not a blocker.
- `svg/mod.rs` gains `curve_tolerance: None` on the Document it builds (SVGs are read without curves) - consistent with the type change.
- The golden moved to wire-iso/wire_dxf_spline_die.nc in `1e9840209` after #3988; its 73 `G3` blocks were unchanged and only the `G1` connector blocks disappeared. I read it; the wire_dxf_selection test is not run here.
- The hand-resolved merge `641ac0448` (arcs.rs) kept both sides; no logic was merged by hand.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
